# Resolve the invocation's own scope. --git-dir is authoritative over
# everything else when present (git's own semantics, verified against
# real git: --git-dir directly names the repository regardless of -C or
# cwd, and wins regardless of option order) -- its value can be entered
# directly, since a .git directory (or worktree gitfile pointer) is
# itself a valid place to run `git branch --show-current` from. Absent
# that, compose every -C value left-to-right (each -C is relative to the
# previous, so this is exactly the `cd ... && cd ...` chain a real shell
# would run), or absent that, the last unconditional `cd` target before
# the invocation. A relative target is resolved against EFFECTIVE_CWD,
# the same base a real shell would start from.
resolve_relative() {
    local base="$1" target="$2"
    if [[ "$target" == /* ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$target"
    else
        printf '%s/%s' "$base" "$target"
    fi
}
